'''Thalanyji''' (also spelt '''Dhalandji''', '''Thalanyji''', and other variations) is an [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] from the [[Pilbara]] region of [[Western Australia]]. It is part of the [[Kanyara languages|Kanyara subgroup]] of the [[Pama–Nyungan languages|Pama–Nyungan language family]].

It is spoken by the [[Thalanyji]] people. It is thought to be [[extinct language|extinct]]; there were six speakers of Thalanyji recorded in 2004/5,<ref name=aiatsisthalanyji>{{AIATSIS|W26|Thalanyji }}</ref> but none since.<ref name=aiatsispinikura>{{AIATSIS|W34|Binigura/Pinikura}}</ref>

According to [[Peter Austin (linguist)|Peter Austin]], [[Pinikura language|Pinikura]], Thalanyji, [[Payungu language|Payungu]] and [[Purduna language|Purdana]] "should probably be classified as belonging to the Kanyara subgroup".<ref name=aiatsispinikura/>
